chapter: First big band, his father, arriving in Kansas City
title: Date of 1936, plans that fell through, and heading for Omaha
summary: The big band was 1936; plans to join a Seattle group fell through, his father died, and he set off for an uncle in Omaha.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Well, did they -- what year was this when you first heard that? I don't mean when you first heard Rush, but when you first heard --
You're 23. Yeah, that's the year of Christopher Columbus, isn't it?

I'm sure that was '36. Because we were -- later on, Howard and myself was supposed to leave and join some group in Seattle, but the deal fell through. So we didn't join this group. So instead, I went back to work in Ark City, went to back to work there, and Howard joined some group -- somebody sent him a ticket from -- wait a minute, wait a minute, because we were talking about it. Somebody sent him a ticket from South -- they were in South Dakota. And we were talking about it just two months ago and I forgot who that was, sent him the ticket.

But anyway, he tried to get me up there to South Dakota with him after I came to Kansas City, you know, because I went to Ark City and only stayed there about two and a half or three weeks and my dad passed and I had to go home to bury my dad and after I came back to the gig -- the gig only lasted about one week, and so, you know how musicians decide, 'Well, where you going to go, man? Are you going to go back home or are you going to go here or are you going to go to Tulsa or --'
The only reason I decided to go to Omaha, I had an uncle in Omaha.
Well, listen, just before you get that far, because that was sad that you lost your dad.
Because your dad -- it seemed to me that I'd read before you told Stanley, he always did want you to go to college, didn't he?
Yes, he was always happy, you know, about me wanting to go to school.
Yeah. Well, but you didn't really get --
